issues.title: doc/rpc-streaming.md and sink doxygen wrongly claim reading a source until it throws…
issues.verdictReason: source_impl<...>::operator() in include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:941-983 only calls con->close_source() when con->stream_receive() itself fails or returns empty (eof); an exception thrown by unmarshall() inside process_one_buffer (called directly, not inside the try/close_source wrapping) propagates to the caller without _source_closed ever being set, so an application that stops reading at that throw, exactly as the new doc text instructs, leaves the stream half open.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-2026-09-29/ironweave/tob-diff-r: The doc (and doc/rpc-streaming.md:110) says reading until it throws closes the source and there is no other way to do it, but source_impl::operator() only calls close_source() on stream_receive failure or eof; if unmarshall() throws inside process_one_buffer, the exception propagates while _source_closed stays false, so an application following the documented contract leaks the stream connection.

issues.title: Back-pressure from a non-reading peer can stall the drain in stream_close()

issues.title: PR description doesn't explain whether the parent client's own unflushed frame is…
issues.verdictReason: The PR body says the incident's core dump showed the same 141-byte compressor frame stuck unflushed on both the stream connection and its parent client, but the fix only touches stream_close(), which is stream-specific. Tracing the parent's normal teardown path (client::loop()'s unconditional call to stop_send_loop() at rpc.cc:1066, which sets _error = true at the very start, before anything else runs) suggests the parent client does not have the same race window that stream_close() had, since sends are refused before the buffer closes rather than after; but confirming that the parent-side symptom in the original incident was a downstream effect rather than an independent bug would need the original core dump or a repro this session cannot access.
issues.scopeReason: Directly bears on whether this PR's fix fully addresses the incident it says it fixes.

reportedAs.mattpocock-review: Parent client's unflushed compressor frame left unexplained by the fix

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-2026-09-29/ironweave/mattpocock: The PR description says the same 141-byte compressor frame was sitting unflushed on both the stream connection and its parent client, but the fix only covers stream connections via stream_close(); it doesn't say whether the parent's pending flush is a separate bug or harmless.
